findings: waitLoaders cancels all tasks then repeatedly processes non-user events until watcher list empty, without deadline. Global counters assert completed+canceled equals started but do not distinguish decode failure from successful image. No actual hang/cancellation timing measured.

loadOne completion updates Media by path, not stale original index, which handles item rotation/deletion better. Noncanceled null-image result increments finished; finished count is not decoded-success count. OOM separately schedules retry.

OOM handler waits current loaders while canceling others, evicts one LRU page then retries/compacts. Global allocator/min-free heuristic and timer are not a hard per-window byte budget or guarantee of recovery. No memory pressure test.

Widget disables delete/delete-all/replace QAction when FlagDisableDelete set. This resolves earlier enforcement uncertainty for those action bindings; rename/move are distinct actions. No UI interaction or alternate slot invocation tested.

Opening window globally suppresses JPEG and ICC log categories, destructor reenables without reference counting multiple windows. Warnings can be hidden or restored while another viewer remains. Error logging is not a per-file complete ledger.
selectItem rejects rowIndex<=0, so requested media on first page cannot be selected by this method, although initial default selection may still pick it. No UI run.

removeSiblings mutates page groups before attempted trash operations and returns on first failure before final UI cleanup/DB removal; partial failure can leave different in-memory/filesystem state. No file mutation performed.
loadMedia evicts while count>5 before adding current page, permitting up to6 tracked pages after append. This is source-level count bound, not measured memory bound; each page variable size.

Benchmark timer waits page isLoaded and reports image count/wall-clock, but has no pixel/decoder oracle and nonreloadable failures can prevent completion. Its logs do not qualify complete-image correctness or production throughput.
